newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-WOOSNAM'S PUTTING IS MYSTERY WRAPPED IN ENIGMA.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOOSNAM'S PUTTING IS MYSTERY WRAPPED IN ENIGMA.

text.p: For Ian Woosnam, putting has always been a mystery wrapped up in an enigma.
He admits freely that he has a love-hate relationship with his putter - whichever one he is using on any particular day.
He concedes that he owns plenty, though some of them don't stay in use for very long.

The little Welshman, who lives on the Channel Island of Jersey, fired a five-under-par 67 in the first round of the British PGA Championship on Friday, thanks in part to a new putter he began using the previous day.
He was asked how many putters he has at home.
"A lot, if they last until I get home," he replied with a grin. "I usually chuck them into the sea on the way."
The latest weapon is a sawn-off version, cut to a length of 32 inches (81 cms) instead of the 34-inch (86 cms) putters he has regularly used.
The shorter club suits the five foot 4-1/2-inch (1.64 metres ) Welshman.
"Some of my putters have been a little bit too long but this one suits me better," he said. "The ball seems to come off the club face better."
It certainly did at the final hole, where he rolled in a monster 55-foot effort for an eagle three - his second of the day.

He had been hoping for a birdie four to finish four under, but it dropped in to leave him just one shot off the lead shared by Irishman Eamonn Darcy and Darren Clarke. They shot 66s, six under for the 6,957-yard Wentworth course.
Woosnam, a former world number one and winner of the U.S. Masters in 1991, says he changes putters frequently. "If it feels okay. I go with it. When it doesn't feel right, I change.
"You do not mind missing putts as long as it feels right. I have been struggling to strike it right all the time.
"I have never had a year when I putted consistently. I have always been a streaky putter."
One of his problems has been that he has a bad back which often rules out practising with the putter. But his back has been better lately and he has been doing his practice on his carpet at home.
Now 39, he says age is a factor. "You twitch a bit as you get older and your confidence is not what it used to be. I'm not a bad putter but sometimes I give it a little twitch."
Woosnam, whose driving right now is fine and whose iron shots are invariably superb, feels he could have a good season if he could get his putting under control.
He has won 31 European titles and 39 worldwide in his career - but none to far in 1997.
"If I'm driving well and hitting my irons as well as I have lately, if I could also putt well I could do what I did last year and win four tournaments," he said.
